Mixture likelihood ratio

Source: R/frns2.R
mixlr.Rd

The weight of a DNA mixture at one locus for one account of who contributed against another. Each account names the alleles of the mixture its known contributors do not explain and the number of unknown contributors who must explain them. Peak heights, drop-out and coancestry are not modelled. See proof("mixlr").

Usage

mixlr(p, np, xp, nd, xd)

Arguments

p

The population frequencies of the alleles in the mixture: named numbers above 0 with a sum of at most 1.

np, nd

The alleles left unexplained under the first and the second account: names of p (or character(0)), at most 20.

xp, xd

The number of unknown contributors under each account.

Value

A named numeric vector: num, den and lr.

Details

With no alleles to explain and one unknown, the denominator is the chance a random person is not excluded from the mixture.

References

Weir, B. S., Triggs, C. M., Starling, L., Stowell, L. I., Walsh, K. A. J. and Buckleton, J. (1997). Interpreting DNA mixtures. Journal of Forensic Sciences, 42(2), 213-222.

Examples

# victim explains a and b; suspect would explain c and d
p <- c(a = 0.1, b = 0.2, c = 0.05, d = 0.15)
mixlr(p, np = character(0), xp = 0, nd = c("c", "d"), xd = 1)
#>      num      den       lr 
#>  1.00000  0.01500 66.66667
